OVERVIEW: WHY NOW (6) starts from the 40m back mark here, but he looks a nice trotter on the rise for team Barker and he’s the horse to beat in the small field of six. He was a mammoth 37.8m winner as favourite at Mount Gambier on Wednesday, and before that started from the same handicap in races at St Arnaud and Hamilton, doing really well in the latter to be beaten just 4.1m by Keayang Minnesota. He’s lightly raced and looks to have the ability to overcome the big handicap. CONNIES PRESIDENT (5) looks the other key contender here off the 20m mark. He ran well for fourth behind Snickers Express at Maryborough last time out, which followed a dominant win from behind the leader at Horsham. He blundered his most recent stand start attempt, but a faultless display will have him right in this. ROBERT JOHN (2) hasn’t done much his last two but the first-up effort when a fast-finishing second at Maryborough was good, while MAORIS RETURN (1) chased home CONNIES PRESIDENT (5) for second here first-up in early October and his next best. BACK: WHY NOW (6) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: WHY NOW (6), CONNIES PRESIDENT (5), ROBERT JOHN (2), MAORIS RETURN (1)

OVERVIEW: SPOOK CROCKER (7) has had plenty of racing in recent days and will line up here for his fourth start since Saturday night. There at Melton, he ran well for fourth behind Captain Moonlight – beaten just 4.8m – and was then well back at Mount Gambier on Wednesday but rounded up most of the field to run second behind Ynobe Nova. The small field suits and he’s a promising type who has won eight of 27 starts. Stablemate OCEAN AVENUE (1) was trapped parked in that same race at the Mount and boxed on for fourth, and his second to the smart Jilliby Sniper at Melton in late October reads well for this, the promising MAJOR ROY (4) sat parked as a warm favourite to win at Ararat latest and all his recent form is sound, while LEWIELEWIS (5) might be the pick of the Aaron Dunn runners based off a good Mildura win and second placing through September. Plenty of hopes! BACK: SPOOK CROCKER (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: SPOOK CROCKER (7), MAJOR ROY (4), OCEAN AVENUE (1), LEWIELEWIS (5)

OVERVIEW: BUILDTHEMANASTATUE (4) led at Melton last week and copped some pressure in front before being grabbed by Ooh Ah Listah, who enjoyed a good run off the pace. It was a sound effort in a slightly higher grade race than this. He enjoyed a fruitful Tasmanian campaign before that with victory in a heat of the Dandy Patch series before a midfield effort in the $75,000 final. If he’s able to work forward and find the top, he should prove hard to beat. SMOKIN STREPO (3) was too far back when fifth at Mount Gambier on Wednesday but was able to run down Normandy Nugget two starts back to win at Ararat and that horse won well at Ballarat this week so the form reads well, SENNA STORM (5) was a dominant winner from the top at Kilmore on November 5 but didn’t do much either side of that, while PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (7) has a sticky draw but good gate speed and was a strong winner from the top at St Arnaud last time out. BACK: BUILDTHEMANASTATUE (4) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BUILDTHEMANASTATUE (4), SMOKIN STREPO (3), SENNA STORM (5), PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (7)

OVERVIEW: Two-year-old SOHO SPARKLE (6) was beaten as a short-priced favourite when she last stepped out at Ballarat back on October 29, but was caught parked there in a 56.2 last half. She ran really well through the Vicbred Super Series, with third placings in the qualifiers behind top-liners Ideal Frankie and Kahula before being well held in the Group 1 final. This is easier and she’s the deserving favourite. I AM MOLLY (7) ran a great race on debut for new trainer Sam Barker at Cranbourne on Sunday after finding the lead and giving expensive yearling purchase Mister Threeofive a real race. She was only beaten 2.5m in a 56.2 last half. She’s a key danger, as is BEACHBOY BRUCE (1), who trialled nicely when second behind five-time winner Rabada recently at Maryborough, and draws for a nice trip first-up. KEAYANG ALABAMA (2) might be next best, but is perhaps more likely a place hope behind the aforementioned rivals. SELECTIONS: SOHO SPARKLE (6), I AM MOLLY (7), BEACHBOY BRUCE (1), KEAYANG ALABAMA (2)

OVERVIEW: Wonderful edition of the Horsham Trotters Cup where you can make a case for a host of horses, notably FOUROUTOFFIVE (9). Nicholas O’Connor’s charge has been racing against some of the best squaregaiters here in Victoria, and arrives here after a ninth placing in the Group 3 Australasian Trotters Championship at Melton last weekend. He finished fifth in the Group 3 Dullard Cup prior to that, and while he’s been well beaten, his efforts are in stronger grade than most of his rivals. He shares the 20m handicap with MEADOW VALLEY STAR (10), but is good enough to overcome it with a faultless display. KEAYANG MINNESOTA (2) starts from the front as she looks to add a fifth-straight win to her recent record, MAXIMEZ (4) finished third in the recent St Arnaud Cup and looked like winning an SA Cup heat before that but galloped in the straight, while IZARRA (5) did a great job to finish fourth there at St Arnaud after an early break. Others can win, including local hope ARTIGAS (3) and MEADOW VALLEY STAR (10). BACK: FOUROUTOFFIVE (9) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: FOUROUTOFFIVE (9), KEAYANG MINNESOTA (2), MAXIMEZ (4), IZARRA (5)

OVERVIEW: BLACK OPAL JACK (9) led and had every chance but was nailed late as favourite at St Arnaud on November 8 by the flying Huxham Chubb, who has now won her last three starts. He had been running well before that and looks one of the key contenders in an even looking 50-55 grade event. BATTON ROUGE (3) sat parked and did a great job to finish second, beaten a head, to Another Woods at Ararat last time, EXOTIC CHESTER (4) has been plain his last four starts but did lead and hold on for second in decent time at Ballarat going back on October 1, while MYDEEPESTDESIRE (8) claimed a well-deserved maiden success last time out at Ararat following great efforts at Maryborough and Melton, and is among the hopes alongside the first-up FAIR CHANCE (6). SELECTIONS: BLACK OPAL JACK (9), BATTON ROUGE (3), EXOTIC CHESTER (4), MYDEEPESTDESIRE (8)

OVERVIEW: This is an historic running of the Horsham Pacing Cup, which will serve as the first standing start race for pacers in Victoria since 2016. And what a competitive field it has drawn! I’m looking towards the backmarkers over the longer trip of 2700m, with Laura Wilson’s top-liner CALEXICO (11) seemingly getting in well with 20m. His last three starts have been strong, with a win at Swan Hill and third placing in track record time behind Storms Collide followed by a midfield finish last weekend in a hot Casey Classic at Melton. He’s a good horse who will be hard to beat. ULTIMATE VINNIE (12) had no luck in the Casey Classic and finished last, but did win a heat before placing third in the final of the recent SA Pacing Cup series at Globe Derby, COASTAL DRIVE (8) was well beaten last time but won a good race at Geelong back in early October and would be a huge threat if he stepped well and worked to the top from his 10m handicap, while CALEXICO’S (11) stablemate ALOT LIKE LOUIE (10) is fresh-up from a break but has trialled nicely and ran some great races in good company last campaign. The chances don’t end there! SELECTIONS: CALEXICO (11), ULTIMATE VINNIE (12), COASTAL DRIVE (8), A LOT LIKE LOUIE (10)

OVERVIEW: Here’s the third heat of the Stawell Pacing Cup, where emergency LOUGLE (1) looks the one to beat if he gains a start from the pole. He sat parked and won heat two of the series at Maryborough on Monday, which followed a race at Melton where he looked the likely winner in the straight before throwing his chances away by breaking and running to the outside fence. He’s a nice pacer on the rise. If he doesn’t start, then things are more open. I’m convinced NEATNTIDY (6) is flying for Aaron Dunn and had absolutely no luck when bolting for a run at Melton last weekend. She had the best closing sectionals in a race before that when seventh behind Jilliby Sniper and arguably should have won another event at the same track in early October but again had no luck. MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (9) ran superbly from last for third in the Swan Hill Pacing Cup before winning at Mildura latest and is a key contender alongside TO THE NINES (11), who rattled home from the tail for fourth behind LOUGLE (1) on Monday. SELECTIONS: LOUGLE (1), NEATNTIDY (6), MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (9), TO THE NINES (11) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R1 #6 WHY NOW (6) – 3 units (win) R2 #7 SPOOK CROCKER – 2 units (win) R3 #4 BUILDTHEMANASTATUE – 3 units (win) R5 #9 FOUROUTOFFIVE – 1 unit (each-way) EARLY QUADDIE 5,6/1,2,4,5,7/3,4,5,7/6,7 QUADDIE 2,4,5,9/3,4,8,9/5,6,8,10,11,12/1,6,9,11 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (1) is resuming but will strip fitter from three recent trial performances with the latest being a second behind SinceIleftyou at Melton. He strikes a very suitable assignment and should take beating. PETITE FOUR (3) has had gait issues in her two starts since resuming but she was able to finish fourth both times. She also finished a distant fourth at the trials last week but could show up if she delivers a fool proof display. NORTHERN SKYE (2) is a fast beginner and is drawn to receive every chance so she cannot be dismissed. CHAMPAGNESALLY (5) has broken stride at her past two attempts to date but she was placed at a Maryborough trial last week so she is worth thought. RINGMERONNIE (6) also galloped when on debut but is a possible improver. SELECTIONS: ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (1), PETITE FOUR (3), NORTHERN SKYE (2), CHAMPAGNESALLY (5)

OVERVIEW:CARPOPHORUS (5) finished strongly when sixth at his Victorian debut, followed with a handy third at Ararat then struck trouble when in a striking position last week. He has performed well enough at his first three local appearances to suggest he is a strong chance in this event. DRESSEDUPINTHECITY (3) is a maiden from 56 starts but she has been getting closer to the money. She finished off well from a nice trailing position when second in a race of similar standard last week. OSCAROO (7) worked home fairly well for third at Maryborough last outing but he wanted to hang in on the corners so the wide draw is a concern. SYNTAX ERROR (4) led out then took cover when third behind Suffarell Hill three starts ago and is likely to try and adopt similar tactics now. She is an experienced maiden but has been trotting consistently in recent times. SELECTIONS: CARPOPHORUS (5), DRESSEDUPINTHECITY (3), OSCAROO (7), SYNTAX ERROR (4)

OVERVIEW: AMALFI (4) is a former New Zealand pacer, which drew poorly and finished unplaced behind King Kasey (won again since) in a heat of the Stawell Cup at his Australian debut. He is better drawn and drops back in class so a better showing is expected. TRYX VIXEN (7) is a fast beginner and has been racing in good form. She progressed forward to race without cover and battled on well for fifth behind Interpretation in a strong race at Kilmore last outing. She is widely drawn again but looms as one of the leading chances. I SEE RED (2) settled in a rearward position and finished off well when fifth at Cranbourne last outing. He is better than his form reads and should make his presence felt. REIGN EM IN (1) is a fast beginner and a short course specialist so he can improve on his numerical form under these conditions. BACK: AMALFI (4) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: AMALFI (4), TRYX VIXEN (7), I SEE RED (2), REIGN EM IN (1)

OVERVIEW: NEDZA THRILLER (4) is a fast beginner and is racing in good form. He led out then took cover and chased hard when a close second at St Arnaud then followed with a third at Maryborough last week, where he attempted to lead throughout. This race is no harder and he should give another forward showing. AI SEDHAI (5) hasn’t been at his best form recently but he will appreciate a drop back in class and he is some chance of finding the lead so an improved showing is expected. ALLWATFUNJINGLES (2) gained a nice trail and finished off well when a close second behind Patnwill at Ballarat. He is drawn to gain a similar trip and should go well again. SILENT REVERIE (7) ran home well for third at Maryborough last week. She usually performs best when she is able to lead and she moves to the front line now so she is worth an investment. COURAGES LAW (8) enjoyed a lovely trip and finished off well for second behind Buckles For Berry then didn’t have much room in the straight at his latest fifth. He is awkwardly drawn but is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: NEDZA THRILLER (4), AI SEDHAI (5), ALLWATFUNJINGLES (2), SILENT REVERIE (7)

OVERVIEW:CRYPTO CROOK (3) settled midfield and finished off stylishly when a game second behind the smart pacer Bettor’s Ideal at Ballarat on Wednesday night. She dashed home and missed out by a slender margin at her debut performance so she appears to be ready to break through for a win. LIGHTNING ORO (9) performed very nicely at the trials prior to galloping shortly after the start and losing her chance on debut. She was looking to be positive early before she broke stride first up and her trial form would indicate she has the ability to test this field. MAKEOVER MIKI (8) is out of the Group 1 winning mare Gumdrops and was driven aggressively mid-race to circle the field and find the front at the 900m when third at a Melton trial effort on Tuesday. He is awkwardly drawn but must be kept safe. JOKIC (1) has performed okay in several recent trial performances and is a possible improver from the pole position. BACK: CRYPTO CROOK (3) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: CRYPTO CROOK (3), LIGHTNING ORO (9), MAKEOVER MIKI (8), JOKIC (1)

OVERVIEW:THE PASO DOBLE (10) broke stride several times and lost his chance at Geelong last outing. He led throughout and scored a runaway win at the trials since and he will take beating if he delivers a fool proof display. SONNYBOY (7) performed below expectations after racing on the outside of the leader throughout when sixth at Cranbourne on Sunday but his form prior was strong. He pushed forward to find the lead and dominated his rivals at Maryborough three starts ago so he is worth another chance. LIFE ON THE HILL (9) struck bother and lost his chance last outing. His form prior was strong and he is worth another chance. MONTANA MUSCLE (3) was doing her best work at the end when fourth behind Lindy Grace last week. She is working back into some form and strikes a suitable assignment now. POPPY POPSTAR (8) hasn’t been at her best form for some time but she is capable of improving under these conditions. SELECTIONS: THE PASO DOBLE (10), SONNYBOY (7), LIFE ON THE HILL (9), MONTANA MUSCLE (3)

OVERVIEW: I CHOOSE YOU (3) is a fast beginner and has been racing well against strong fields. He progressed forward to race without cover and battled on strongly for third behind Pass The Salt last outing so he will take catching if he can find the lead. DEEJAY DEX (11) was confidently supported and ran a very good race after a slow beginning when a close third behind Aetos Dynamis at Shepparton last outing. He is a risky beginner but will be competitive if he can get away safely. BUSLIN BRODY (1) can also be a little awkward at the start but he sustained a strong run from the 600m when a game second at Kilmore last outing so he is not without a chance. CHAMPAGNES (10) performs best when she is close to the speed so being drawn on the second line is a disadvantage but she did defeat a field of similar standard at Maryborough on October 30 so she cannot be left out of calculations. BACK: I CHOOSE YOU (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: I CHOOSE YOU (3), DEEJAY DEX (11), BUSLIN BRODY (1), CHAMPAGNES (10)

OVERVIEW: KENNYWOULD (11) has been racing really well against strong fields under the standing start conditions and led throughout to win the St Arnaud Cup at his latest attempt. It is different conditions this afternoon but it is a suitable line up so he must be respected. PARIS KAY (8) is awkwardly drawn but is racing well enough to figure in the finish. She was runner up in the Swan Hill Cup after doing plenty of chasing on October 15 and was runner up under similar conditions last week. SOVEREIGN TIGER (2) is a fast beginner and won over Zarski (won since) after finding the back on the leader at Kilmore five starts ago. He is ideally drawn to suit his racing pattern and should go well. OLIVER SMUDGE (10) faces a significant rise in class and is meeting some Metropolitan horses at only his fourth career start but he does appear to be a promising type so he cannot be underestimated. SELECTIONS: KENNYWOULD (11), PARIS KAY (8), SOVEREIGN TIGER (2), OLIVER SMUDGE (10)

OVERVIEW: MY FATAL CHARM (10) has performed very well in two starts since coming from Tasmania and is ready to break through for a win. She was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished quickly via the sprint lane when a close second behind Piastri last outing. BUBBLE OVER (9) was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off well for fifth at her latest appearance. She has returned from a spell in peak form and is worth an investment. BRAVE ART (8) is stepping up in class from her recent performances but she has been impressive recently. She led throughout and dashed home in a slick final half of 56.6 seconds to win comfortably at Maryborough last week. BETTOR DOO (3) trailed the leader Presidentialchange and just failed to run him down in what was simply a sprint up the home straight at St Arnaud. He has won two of his past five starts and should go well again. ANIMADO (6) is a versatile pacer and is steadily working back to his best form so he is worth an investment. BACK: MY FATAL CHARM (10) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: MY FATAL CHARM (10), BUBBLE OVER (9), BRAVE ART (8), BETTOR DOO (3)

OVERVIEW:THEBUCKSONYOU (8) is a handy 4yo pacer, which is resuming since a fifth at Mildura in August. He is versatile and beat a reasonable field at a Swan Hill victory towards the end of his last campaign so he must be respected. SHIRLEY NOT (7) won twice at Mildura in October and has the perfect trailing draw behind MIDNIGHT PIRATE (1) so she cannot be left out of calculations. She was held up for a run at a vital stage and chased hard for second on Thursday night. MIDNIGHT PIRATE (1) defeated an easier field on Thursday night but he kicked well clear at the 400m and sustained the run so he is worth thought from the pole position. MAGGACIS (2) endured a wide trip in the final circuit and battled on well when resuming on Thursday night. He should be fitter and is better drawn so he is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: THEBUCKSONYOU (8), SHIRLEY NOT (7), MIDNIGHT PIRATE (1), MAGGACIS (2)

OVERVIEW:THE LADYBIRD (11) settled in the second half of the field, angled wide in the home straight and finished off quickly for an eye-catching third at Shepparton last week. She gained a nice trail and got home best to win at Mildura prior so she is worth thought again. THE IRISHMAN (8) has been placed at his past four attempts and should be competitive against this class. He raced without cover throughout and battled on strongly for third at Mount Gambier last outing. PUNTO CALIENTE (7) ran home strongly from last and did well at Mildura on Thursday night. He is awkwardly drawn but should be hitting the line strongly again. WATCHING OVER US (6) finished off well for second behind THE LADYBIRD (11) on November 10. He was driven very aggressively in the early stages and peaked at the end on Thursday night but his efforts from off the speed prior were sound. DIAMOND KRUSHER (5) and GROVE DALE (2) are both fast beginners and are drawn to be prominent over sprint distance. SELECTIONS: THE LADYBIRD (11), THE IRISHMAN (8), PUNTO CALIENTE (7), WATCHING OVER US (6)

OVERVIEW: DALLAS MIKI (7) is a strong staying type that performs best when he is able to lead so he couldn’t have drawn worse. He progressed forward to find the front and dominated his rivals two starts ago and he has the class to test this field. He was gunned down by KYORETSU (8) on Thursday night but the extra distance of this event is in his favour. KYORETSU (8) began quickly, raced roughly and did well to remain pacing on the first turn to trail the leader and was very quick at the end when he won on Thursday night. He drops back to the second line now but should prove hard to beat again. NAROBI (2) is a South Australian trained mare that is making her Mildura debut. She has been racing consistently and trainer Peter Bain boasts a good strike rate at Mildura so she must be respected. PRIORITISE (6) sustained a long run to beat a field of similar quality on October 20. He has had a horror run with the barrier draw but he was placed under similar conditions on Thursday night and continues to perform strongly so he cannot be dismissed. SELECTIONS: DALLAS MIKI (7), KYORETSU (8), NAROBI (2), PRIORITISE (6)

OVERVIEW: SPRINGFIELD RIVER (6) joins trainer John Tormey and will appreciate a significant drop back in class for this assignment. He is versatile and is capable of running fast time so he warrants respect. CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (3) attempted to lead throughout when second at Mildura on Thursday night. He is drawn to obtain a prominent position again and looms as one of the leading chances. ACCELERE (5) is a fast beginner and performs best when he is able to lead. He has created a good impression at Mildura with a string of consistent performances and another bold showing is expected. He left a trailing position to park without cover and didn’t have a great deal of luck on Thursday night. ROJENBYE (1) finished off solidly from midfield to get up and defeat My Ultimate Rudi at Mildura on November 06. He is likely to gain an economical run from the ideal draw and is worth thought again, despite performing well below expectations on Thursday night. BACK: SPRINGFIELD RIVER (6) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: SPRINGFIELD RIVER (6), CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (3), ACCELERE (5), ROJENBYE (1)

OVERVIEW:CAULONIA TERROR (4) is capable of sprinting to the line quickly with the right trail forward as evidenced by his big victory at Mildura on Thursday night. He has struck peak form and will take beating again. OZZIE DAYBREAK (7) has been racing well but without luck and gets his chance to run a big race with the perfect trailing draw behind the likely leader HOOKLINEANDSINKER (1). He performed nicely again on Thursday night having worked into third at the end. G B BRAVE (3) ran home nicely for a game second when resuming on Thursday night and is worth a ticket each way. CALF PEN (5) ran a big race when he moved up without cover and went down fighting when second behind Bettorbust on November 06. He was driven aggressively early and raced fiercely thereafter so he had excuses on Thursday night. He continues to perform strongly against this class and should give another bold showing. HOOKLINEANDSINKER (1) hasn’t been at his best form recently but he tends to excel when he is able to lead over the sprint distance so he has the conditions to suit him here. SELECTIONS: CAULONIA TERROR (4), OZZIE DAYBREAK (7),G B BRAVE (3), CALF PEN (5)

OVERVIEW:EVA EXPRESS (6) led out then took cover when a close second behind Mystic Motiver in a stronger race at Kilmore two starts ago. She was caught wide early and had to be restrained to last from a similar poor draw on Thursday night but will find this to be a suitable assignment and should take tossing. SWEET LUCY LOU (5) possesses early speed and is a good chance of finding the lead. She raced without cover throughout at her latest fourth and should be competitive against this line up. LITLMAX (7) was confidently driven and showed promise when second on debut. She didn’t have much luck at her next few attempts and went down fighting after racing without cover on Thursday night so she could gain her maiden success at short notice. DARK AT MIDNIGHT (3) is a first starter for trainer Andrew Vozlic, which finished a distant third at his only trial performance. He is nicely drawn first up so he must be kept safe. SELECTIONS: EVA EXPRESS (6), SWEET LUCY LOU (5), LITLMAX (7), DARK AT MIDNIGHT (3)

OVERVIEW: OUR MONARCH (5) was heavily supported and was run down in the last stride when attempting to lead throughout at her debut performance. She should have benefited from that experience and is capable of going one better. BETTY CAROLINE (2) left the position behind the leader to race without cover when a brave second at Mildura last week. She is ideally drawn and should run a big race again. CRUEL MISTRESS (7) is an experienced maiden having had 33 attempts but she is getting closer to the money. She raced without cover when a game second behind Cheddar Cheese on November 06 and was the runner up again at Mildura on Thursday night. SANTA CASA LEVI (3) was checked with 700m remaining and lost approximately four lengths when unplaced on Thursday night and is a possible improver from his good draw. BACK: OUR MONARCH (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: OUR MONARCH (5), BETTY CAROLINE (2), CRUEL MISTRESS (7), SANTA CASA LEVI (3)

OVERVIEW: WINSHEMAY (3) followed some good trial performances with a soft debut victory then was spelled. She finished strongly from a long way back when third on resumption and she appears to have a promising future. MY ULTIMATE HENRY (5) progressed forward to find the lead, ran along at a genuine tempo and was run down late in fast time on Thursday night. He is racing well and looms as one of the leading chances again. SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (6) has done well in three local starts and should make his presence felt. He was a runaway winner on November 06 then attempted to lead throughout and was run down by the handy South Australian pacer Hilltop Crunch at his latest second. TAMALIA (1) was placed after trailing the leader at St Arnaud on November 08 and she led throughout to beat easier opposition on Thursday night. She is drawn to suit her racing pattern and may be able to take the next step forward. KAIDENBOY (2) makes his debut for trainer Kate Attard and took on a stronger field at his latest Ararat fifth. He has claims along with CLARENDEN ARCADIA (4). BACK: WINSHEMAY (3) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: WINSHEMAY (3), MY ULTIMATE HENRY (5), SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (6), TAMALIA (1)

OVERVIEW: HESASTAR (6) is the one of only two horses in this event that did not contest the meeting at Mildura on Thursday so he comes into the race with fresh legs. He was driven aggressively from the same draw and was able to score after racing without cover throughout in a field of similar quality last outing so he will prove very hard to beat again. EAGLEYE (4) was a late withdrawal on Thursday night but his overall form has been sound and he strikes a suitable assignment now. INDIANAS SON (5) settled midfield and held his ground over the latter stages at Mildura on Thursday. The small field will assist his chances and he is capable of filling a place. THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (3) was driven for early speed but couldn’t get across to the markers and was shuffled back in the field mid-race so he didn’t enjoy the best of luck at Mildura on Thursday. He gets his chance to improve under these conditions. THE AFRICAN QUEEN (2) gained a nice trail and battled into a distant fourth on Thursday night. She is a place chance from her good draw. BACK: HESASTAR (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: HESASTAR (6), EAGLEYE (4), INDIANAS SON (5), THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (3)

OVERVIEW: Just the three runners in the APG feature for the 3yo fillies. ORLANDO VEYRON (1) is the clear standout based on her race experience and placings behind high-quality trotters in her age group. She has sound manners and good gate speed to lead and take control here. She was a winner last start, beating the only danger in this. The only way she doesn't win is if she beats herself with bad manners, but she should be prohibitive odds. THE WOOL BROKER (2) is the only other runner with race experience and ran 3rd to the top pick at her last start. She was a winner three runs back in slow time at Geelong. Considering she's likely to be on the leader's back, with what's anticipated to be a clear lack of pace or pressure, she'll be relying on the polemarker not being on her game. WHIRLWIN (3) is an NSW visitor making her debut on the back of seven trials, where she's been beaten by sizeable margins and has often done things wrong. She's from an astute stable, which could present some upside, but I'm happy to dismiss her at this stage. SELECTIONS:ORLANDO VEYRON (1), THE WOOL BROKER (2), WHIRLWIN (3)

OVERVIEW:SEW HOPEFULL (1) is a 3yo filly and a 24-start maiden, but all indications from her last five starts, particularly her latest outing, suggest a win is very close. She was able to lead from the outside barrier at Geelong and showed plenty of guts, only narrowly beaten by the long odds-on favourite. She can lead these over the short trip and potentially provide legendary Lance Justice with his first winning drive since his comeback last week. BEAU BECA (8) looks likely to catch her back, map well over the short trip and get her chance along the passing lane. She's been racing consistently in her past few starts, and this presents as her most suitable set-up in some time. SURETHING (4) is a 2yo filly taking on more experienced types but has displayed some ability in her four career runs, winning once and missing a place only once. This isn't an overly strong race despite her inexperience. GOZO SWEET (3) should be fitter here second up from a break and was a winner last preparation against similar types. She should map well to be in the mix. BAD GRANDMA (2), LOOK AT HER (5) and ROCK POSTER (10) all have claims for the minor money. SELECTIONS:SEW HOPEFULL (1), BEAU BECA (8), SURETHING (4), GOZO SWEET (3)

OVERVIEW: Two heats leading into a final, with last week's Geelong race looking the better reference on time. MY ATLANTIS (3) won the Geelong race and really had to earn it, coming from last and sustaining a three-wide run for the final lap in solid enough time. He's been a lightly raced 7yo, but he's enjoying his best season and is going for three in a row here. The soft draw helps offset his lack of tactical speed, allowing him to come with one run late and be strong over the final 100m. MONSIEUR FLAMEL (6) raced in both heats, coming off the speed to finish 3rd before leading at Geelong, where he looked to have every chance as an odds-on favourite, only to be run down right on the post. The lead may be there again, so he'll be in it for a long way. LIKE A GAZELLE (4) could represent some value as the likely map horse, given she can show speed and take cover to get her chance along the sprint lane. She narrowly missed here at Melton when adopting those tactics. BREATHE EASY (7) has a tough draw but may float forward to get in front of some key rivals and has an SP profile worth respecting. SPORTS NARRATOR (10) and COOL STORY (11) were both heat winners here at Melton, but this sets up very differently with the tough draws they must overcome. They'll need the tempo on to come with one run. OUR BELLA LUCIA (2) and QUICK CRUNCH (9) have soft trailing draws that could see them improve on previous efforts, but I prefer them for the minor money. BACK: MY ATLANTIS (3) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:MY ATLANTIS (3), MONSIEUR FLAMEL (6), LIKE A GAZELLE (4), COOL STORY (11)

OVERVIEW: Another series of heats leading into a final, this time for the trotters. DOSSIER (9) returned to form, spanking them in her heat from the same draw, where she trailed through to map well before running away from the field. To be fair, the performance looked better to the eye than on the clock. Chris Alford sticking with her is a big plus. QUAKE PROOF (8) is at his best when he can coil up after doing no work and let down with one run when the others are getting tired. That was the case in his heat victory, where he came from last and swept wide. He'll have to navigate a passage this time but can hit the line when the breaks come. JAKARTA (11) ran well in both heats and will appreciate what looks to be a speedy front line to work into the race strongly late. That speed on the front line comes from CHINSKI (1), DESERT ASSASIN (2), KIMBERLYS TREE (3), APRIL SUN (5), JOE LOU (6) and LEANNE LEEANN (7), who all regularly press forward or like to lead in their races. There could be plenty of jostling for that position, making the map difficult to predict and their winning chances equally uncertain. BACK: DOSSIER (9) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:DOSSIER (9), QUAKE PROOF (8), JAKARTA (11), LEANNE LEEANN (7)

OVERVIEW:JILLIBY UTAH (3) finds a suitable race and looks ready to win based on what he's displayed over the past couple of months, where he's taken on stronger types and hasn't been too far away. He has good early gate speed, which he showed last start at Geelong, only to be double-crossed before finishing solidly when clear. He can lead these over the short trip, and Ewa Justice, one of the leading drivers this season, jumps on. CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (10) has shown good ability, finishing runner-up on five occasions from nine starts, but he was a little plain last time, which is a concern, and he does have a tricky draw to overcome. His best is good enough. RETRO FIT (8) found the line well last time for a 2nd at Melton in a race many of these contested. She has a soft draw and can finish strongly with the right tempo. DYGNALI (2) has a solid SP profile, a soft draw and a good driver to help improve on recent outings. WICKED ONE (1) needs to lift slightly but looks to map very well, so could be a knockout chance with an economical trip. BACK: JILLIBY UTAH (3) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:JILLIBY UTAH (3), CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (10), RETRO FIT (8), WICKED ONE (1)

OVERVIEW:KING SAINT (8) could be a big improver here and represent some value, dropping well back in class and finally appearing to get a suitable set-up. He draws behind a runner who always likes to lead, with the likelihood that he can catch his back over the short trip and get his chance along the passing lane. The last time he raced in this ratings band, he was a winner. HAPPILY (2) found the going a bit too slick last time in a good-quality race at Geelong, where she had every chance to finish 4th. Her form prior was very good, running well even when taking on some smart ones, but when she dropped back to a suitable grade, she was a winner. She's right in it. HELLOVATIME (1) runs his best races when able to lead, and although he's done so recently, it's been against tougher opposition than he meets here. His overall record this season is good in similar conditions. PISTOL PEARCE (6) was my best bet last Saturday night at Melton, but on face value, he was disappointing and had every chance. His two runs prior were excellent if you're prepared to forgive that effort. POPCORNFRIDAY (3) is a recent Melton winner, so can't be dismissed, while any betting moves for INVITATION ONLY (4) need to be respected off some decent trials. He returns to his former stable, where he won better races at this track. BACK: KING SAINT (8) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:KING SAINT (8), HAPPILY (2), HELLOVATIME (1), PISTOL PEARCE (6)

OVERVIEW:PRECIOUS BELLE (3) is a mare who always needs luck and the right tempo, as she maps negatively and likes to come with one run. As a result, she often races better at this track, where there's usually a more genuine speed than what she can face at tighter provincial tracks. There's a strong likelihood the leaders won't be able to put down a slick last half, so swoopers are favoured. ARE WEASLEY (9) goes to a back-row draw after some solid efforts when able to map favourably. His overall form is better than most, so he warrants respect. ROBLEN RANGER (8) was disappointing last start, but if you're prepared to overlook that effort, his form prior was good for a race of this calibre. He maps behind the likely leader and can finish off well. FLIGHT LOUTENANT (7) comes out of a winnable race last time, where he still did things wrong but was able to score. He gets no map favours here, but an astute trainer/driver combination commands respect. PICKLE IT (1) looks the leader but needs to improve, while AVIERO (5) and HURRICANE HOOLEY (6) are grinding types who are often thereabouts in these races for the minor money. SELECTIONS:PRECIOUS BELLE (3), ARE WEASLEY (9), ROBLEN RANGER (8), FLIGHT LOUTENANT (7)

OVERVIEW:WAR ZONE (9) is first up here and has proven himself to be a handy 3yo, delivering some big wins, albeit when he's been able to lead. That was the case at this track earlier in the year, where he put a space on his rivals, some of whom he meets again here. He's had one winning trial leading into this, and while fitness and the draw are against him, the anticipated early tempo and his good record with Justice are positives. TUKARUA (6) is a fast beginner and was terrific in winning first up, defeating a subsequent winner who has since franked the form. She was also a winner at this track from the back row, beating some rivals she faces here. The only concern is the map, as although she has speed, so too do several others drawn to her inside. YANKEE GAMBLER (1) is always honest at this level, but he's not known for producing a sharp sprint at the end of his races. That makes the draw a slight negative, as he looks likely to be crossed. MIDNIGHT MOJO (4) is consistent in these types of races, aided by her tactical speed to find a suitable trip here. She's honest enough to consider. WOODLEA DIEGO (3) is a quick beginner who will be looking for the top end, as will ROSBERG (5), who had every chance last Sunday at Cranbourne when able to lead. SNACK LOVER (8) gets a soft run and could be the one to flash late if they overcook things. It's an open race. SELECTIONS:WAR ZONE (9), TUKARUA (6), YANKEE GAMBLER (1), MIDNIGHT MOJO (4)

OVERVIEW:OUR TRUE COLOURS (8) finds the most suitable race she's been in for a long time, and what stands out is her record at Melton compared to the opposition. She boasts four wins at the track and plenty of experience in better-quality races. She's an opportunist, so the soft draw is no disadvantage, particularly with the accomplished John Caldow navigating a path when the others are tiring. TASTE IT (9) is known for liking to lead, but she was a winner two runs back coming off the pace, which is particularly encouraging considering the depth of opposition. The trailing draw should see her map well enough to work into the race at the right time. ENABLE ME (7) has a tough draw to overcome but looks well suited on the ratings scale and is more capable of running slicker times than the majority of the opposition. DOT BALL (6) doesn't win out of turn, but similar to the ones already mentioned, looks to have found the weakest race for some time and has the potential to be more map-positive than most. ROCKNROLL RAMBO (4) locked wheels at a key stage last time and has minor claims for first fours with the right run, along with IMAGUNNARESTNGO (2) and GOODTIME MAE (5). SELECTIONS:OUR TRUE COLOURS (8), TASTE IT (9), ENABLE ME (7), DOT BALL (6)

OVERVIEW: Exact race conditions as the previous, where the form is nothing to write home about. FREAK OUT (8) has performed well at this track in the past and often gets caught doing plenty of work in his races. This draw allows him to spend fewer tickets early and save them for late when the others are weakening. ICANMOTOR (3) narrowly missed last start and gets a more favourable draw now. Leedham is a driver who wins with regularity at this track, which is a positive factor. ALLHEARTNOHEIGHT (7) can be a little hard to catch but has performances at this track that stack up in a race of this calibre. Despite the wide draw, she comes into calculations. SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) can take advantage of this draw and look for the lead, which is advantageous over the short trip. He's yet to place from seven attempts at this track, however. ALCATRAZ GIRL (4) was able to lead and looked to have every chance last start at Shepparton. She's map-dependent, but keep her safe. SELECTIONS:FREAK OUT (8), ICANMOTOR (3), SIR CANDY CLOUD (1), ALLHEARTNOHEIGHT (7)

OVERVIEW: COLTRANE (1) remains a risky conveyance at this stage of his career, but I’m convinced there’s a stack of ability there and a faultless display – as unlikely as it might be – would see him right in this clash from the good draw. He made a mistake and took no part in his last start at Maryborough when well fancied in a race a few of these contested won by LORD LOGAN (9), which came after an unlucky first-up run behind that same horse at Geelong and dominant win at Melton in easier grade. I’m happy to take a chance if he comes up each-way odds. I DREAM OF MILLIE (2) looks the likely early leader and must rate as a good chance based off back-to-back runner-up placings in the St Arnaud Trotters Cup and Matchmaker Mile in recent starts, TICTOK (4) is running so consistently well of late and just needs the breaks to come her way to be a factor, while the talented KYVALLEY MICHAEL (8), NAKEDTRUTH (10), who was only nailed late last weekend by Aldebaran Sue, and LORD LOGAN (9), who is shooting for three-straight triumphs, are the other key contenders in a wide-open clash to commence the night at Melton. BACK: COLTRANE (1) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: COLTRANE (1), I DREAM OF MILLIE (2), TICTOK (4), KYVALLEY MICHAEL (8)

OVERVIEW: Former Queensland and South Australian-based pacer OUR INDIFFERENCE (1) is first-up here in Victoria for Jodi Quinlan and looks to be a major player in this clash for horses who have not won a race with advertised stakemoney of $15,000 or more. He trialled in a slick last half of 55.8 at Melton on November 10, and has run some nice races at Globe Derby in recent times. He’s a quick beginner who could either lead or get a nice trip behind fellow fast starters BANDIT EYES (2) or MAAS BETTING AGAIN (3), and from there he’d be a good chance as the clear ratings topper at NR89. STEEL THE MOMENT (5) didn’t have much luck in the straight and can be forgiven for beating just one rival home last weekend with his prior form reading well for a race like this, BETTORLEFTALONE (8) was twice rolled as favourite by stablemate REFUSAL (10) before breaking through in a suitable race from the top at Shepparton on Tuesday and draws for a good trip, while BANDIT EYES (2) would be a huge factor if he found the fence given he led and won by a huge margin in good time here at Melton on August 29. Most of the others can win with the right trip, too! SELECTIONS: OUR INDIFFERENCE (1), STEEL THE MOMENT (5), BETTORLEFTALONE (8), BANDIT EYES (2)

OVERVIEW: Fast class pace of the night brings a very nice field together where SEATHESTARS (6) is fancied for a return to the winner’s stall. He worked to the top and held off MY LITTLE BO (5) at Melton on October 24, then ran a brave third to the very smart Fairplay before cutting late ground off Brooklyn Dan last Saturday night in a slick 26.5 last quarter. He’s a smart horse on the rise! GOLDEN TRIBE (8) is a similar talent first-up from a break here on the back of a NSW campaign and two good lead-up trials at Terang. The inside back row draw is a little sticky, but he’s good enough. MY LITTLE BO (5) led and held off MIGHTY JOLT (2) over this track and trip last time to score but this does look harder, while I fancied OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (3) would run really well last weekend but he was caught parked and dropped out badly. It’s often worth forgiving one bad performance and his prior form was outstanding with good runs behind superstar Bettor Beach, Komodo and SEATHESTARS (6). SELECTIONS: SEATHESTARS (6), GOLDEN TRIBE (8), MY LITTLE BO (5), OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (3)

OVERVIEW: Thinking SHAZZA LOVE (1) might be able to lead here from the good draw and that would give three-year-old SOLS ME NAME (8) a great chance of victory. He was well fancied when favourite first-up at Melton on November 11 but was caught parked there and ultimately faded into third. He’s a lightly-raced type from the Jayne Davies barn with good speed, so will be very hard to hold out late. His close-up fourth in a hot 3YO race during June behind Luvtobeuptome, Most Exciting and Le Cardinal looks nice on paper. SHAZZA LOVE (1) hasn’t really been a threat of late but can improve sharply drawn the inside over the 1720m, LAMBRO MACH (9) hasn’t raced since late September but is a very capable pacer who should get a nice run in the small field, while EL LAZZAR (5) has been a real find for trainer Lochie Cook with four wins from seven starts and heads here after a serviceable effort from out the back in a good race last Saturday night. BACK: SOLS ME NAME (8) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: SOLS ME NAME (8), SHAZZA LOVE (1), LAMBRO MACH (9), EL LAZZAR (5)

OVERVIEW: Fascinating race with a fascinating speed map where I’ll lean towards CHARLESTON AVENUE (2), who looks a real talent on the rise for the Chris Svanosio stable. He ran well from bad gates and with little luck his last two, which followed two impressive wins at Cranbourne and Maryborough. He isn’t drawn to find the fence, which is a concern in a good race, but I’ve just been really taken with him recently and I’m happy to be in his corner. HOWDY MATE (4) was favourite for the Group 1 Victoria Trotters Derby on November 1 and ran well despite being beaten 9.3m into sixth. He’s already a three-year-old Group 1 Vicbred winner this season, so is certainly a key player here. KEAYANG KURKI (5) ran a cracker to win the Matchmaker Mile at Maryborough, which followed a really good effort when narrowly beaten by the in-form RUBYS DREAM (7) at Melton prior. Those two are among the many gate speed runners here. CENTURION DREAM (1) draws well and can certainly be dangerous with the right trip, while KYVALLEY MAVEN (6) is first-up back in the care of Svanosio and is a talented squaregaiter who wouldn’t surprise at his best. BACK: CHARLESTON AVENUE (2) – 1.5 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: CHARLESTON AVENUE (2), HOWDY MATE (4), KEAYANG KURKI (5), CENTURION DREAM (1)

OVERVIEW: Tricky race, but EARL OF PEMBROKE (1) might be the safest way to play from the good barrier one draw. He has the speed to hold a prominent position, and while his recent form isn’t anything incredible, he did win a nice race coming from last here at Melton back on October 9. TWISTING BY (6) presents third-up following two sound efforts at Melton and will be hitting the line hard from back in the field if the tempo is genuine, KEAYANG VIPER (8) is the sole runner on the back row and is a progressive mare from the Lee stable who has won six races this season, while LUVA SCRAP (4) performed really well when second to King Kasey first-up from a spell at Ararat on November 9, and that horse has won again since to frank the form. Opportunist CLYMENUS (5) and talented GUNFORHIRE (7) are the others worth considering in Quaddies. SELECTIONS: EARL OF PEMBROKE (1), TWISTING BY (6), KEAYANG VIPER (8), LUVA SCRAP (4)

OVERVIEW: YANKEE RAIN (8) has been a lovely recruit for young trainer Tom Rundle, who has produced the four-year-old mare for four wins from eight starts this season. She heads here on the back of an easy front-running success at St Arnaud, which followed a death-seat triumph in a good last half at Ballarat. The inside back row draw is a little worry, but the 2240m journey gives driver Glen Craven time to work off the fence and his charge should be fighting out the finish. MASTER LOUEY (5) endured a tough trip as favourite last Friday at Melton when he locked wheels and did a power of work in the last lap before fading late, but his prior win at Ballarat was good from the front. He’s a key player once again. OOH AH LISTAH (6) backed up a couple of good efforts with a deserved win in a suitable race at Melton on November 11, while JUSJOHN (3) has the speed to find the top and could be a sharp improver second-up after a sound return at Geelong last Friday. MISTER AMERICANO (9) and even ROBLEN DEMON (2) at big odds are others to consider. SELECTIONS: YANKEE RAIN (8), MASTER LOUEY (5), OOH AH LISTAH (6), JUSJOHN (3)

OVERVIEW: YETTI (7) looks very well placed in this 0-1 win event for the trotters. He is second-up from a break after racing at Ballarat on Wednesday night when he trotted roughly and ultimately failed to beat a rival home. Late last preparation, he landed an impressive maiden win at the same track when he galloped early, tacked on and rounded up the field for a soft victory. He’s also trialled nicely at Terang recently and looks hard to beat. CARTACALHA (5) looks a key danger in a race with not much form to get overly excited about. He was caught parked at Maryborough last time out and hit the front before being well beaten by Glorified, but did well to hold third. It followed some other serviceable efforts at Ballarat and Kilmore, and he’s good enough to score a second career victory here. ASONGOFTHEHEART (8) is a nice three-year-old for Katrina Fitzpatrick who ran home okay for sixth at Maryborough on Monday and wouldn’t surprise, while JUST ME AND YOU (3) might be next best, but they could all sneak into the minor end of the prize without shocking. BACK: YETTI (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: YETTI (7), CARTACALHA (5), ASONGOFTHEHEART (8), JUST ME AND YOU (3) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R1 #1 COLTRANE – 1 unit (each-way) R4 #8 SOLS ME NAME – 3 units (win) R5 #2 CHARLESTON AVENUE – 1.5 units (each-way) R8 #7 YETTI – 2 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 1,2,4,8,9,10/1,2,4,5,8/5,6,8/1,5,8,9 QUADDIE 1,2,4,5,7/1,4,5,6,8/5,6,8/5,7,8 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

THE BOTTLEMART STOCKADE There was plenty of merit in last week's resuming performance of THE NITESHIFT (1) when he led from this barrier and stuck on well for a 1.6m second. The distance rise is some query but he owns a strong record here and won his lone second-up attempt so should be improved. WICKED CONFESSION (3) came from this barrier when less than 6m behind The Nightshift in fourth last week and beat some good mares in winning here prior. First try at this distance but she is going well. GUNNA RELOAD (2) draws much better than when second to Wicked Confession last start and won both rounds of the Breeders Challenge 4M series prior. Races well at this longer distance so is a player. JUNGLE DRAGON (8) draws wide but was brave last week, sticking on to place after racing parked. Respect. SINALOA (7) has had no luck when caught wide in both starts since placing here. Include.

NUTRIEN EQUINE NSW BREEDERS CHALLENGE BLUE - 3YO FILLIES FINAL (GROUP 2) ONE MORE REASON (6) was far too good in her qualifier, leading from a couple of spots wider than this before going on to score by close to 5m. That continued her consistent form at this circuit and distance, highlighted by her Group 1 placing in the Breeders Challenge final when only 5m off record-breaking filly Ark Sea. That looks very strong form for this. Victorian filly ROCKNROLL WILLOW (8) stretched her winning run to four when she proved too good at this circuit and distance first up. A wider draw makes this tougher but she is two from two when second-up so should be improved. FAKE FRIENDS (5) led from wider and stuck on for second to Rocknroll Willow in the heats. Draws inside that rival this time so can be prominent as can OSHLEY (4) who draws much better than when she raced three wide without cover to stuck on to place behind One More Reason last start. THE ATTRACTOR (2) has exotic claims from a low draw.

NUTRIEN EQUINE NSW BREEDERS CHALLENGE BLUE - 2YO FILLIES FINAL (GROUP 2) Looks a race in two and the draw makes for an intriguing clash. COMEANDSEE (5) made it four from four this time in when leading and dominating her heat last start. Beat main rival Birdsong to win the Group 1 Breeders Challenge 2F Final two back but draws outside her this time in. That creates more of a challenge but she has the early speed to go forward again and is unbeaten at the mile. BIRDSONG (1) was only 4m behind Comeandsee in that Breeders Challenge final after drawing wide and racing parked but sticking on well. That was her lone defeat in five runs this campaign, all of them at this circuit and distance. Talented and the ace draw gives her a big shot at turning the tables. YOUR SHUFFLE (2) was an eye-catching fourth behind the top-two in that final two back when she drew widest and went back but closed late. Draws low so is worth including along with GUNNAREASON (8) and SHES A SWINGA (11) who both draw wide but come off seconds to the top two picks in the heats.

NUTRIEN EQUINE NSW BREEDERS CHALLENGE BLUE - 3YO COLTS & GELDINGS FINAL (GROUP 2) LEWIE KELLY (4) was a class above his rivals in his qualifier, talking advantage of the ace draw to lead before cruising home by close to 31m. Draws a couple of spots wider but has gate speed so can go forward again. Only needs to hold that form and he'll be very hard to catch. LEXY (12) has come from back row draws for close seconds in his last two starts, the latest at this circuit and distance when he raced three wide without cover but fought well to go under by a head. Cops another tough barrier but he is going well. YA RACIN CARL (10) took his strike rate at this circuit and distance to 50 per cent when he led from a similar draw and dug deep to beat Lexy last time. Can be prominent again. COWBOY CULTURE (8) was no match for Lewie Kelly last start but he drew deep and raced wide before boxing on for second. Draws a little lower so he could get into the finish. THE WICKED WARRIOR (2) placed after racing wide last start. Could be competitive from the low draw.

TAB LEN SMITH MILE (GROUP 1) A break proved costly for KINGMAN (3) when attempting to defend his NZ Cup title at Addington last week but he was building nicely prior with two strong efforts behind Captains Mistress, finishing fourth from the back line in the Victoria Cup and coming from a similar barrier to this for a 4m second to the star mare the last time he raced here. That result is a good pointer to this. HI MANAMEISJEFF (7) has been targeting this race and is in peak form at the right time with back-to-back wins at this circuit and distance, leading from this barrier to cruise home last week. He is a Menangle specialist and this looks his chance to land the Group 1 he deserves. DANGEROUS (10) was no match for Hi Manameisjeff as runner-up last week and draws wide again but he was first up for four weeks there so may be improved and did kick off the campaign with back to-back wins at the circuit and distance. BULLETPROOF BOY (4) won the Newcastle Mile the last time he came to NSW. respect from a good draw.

THE TAB EUREKA (GROUP 1) THE LAST TRIP (9) has enjoyed the perfect lead-up to this and had a taste of the circuit when he led from a similar draw to score well last start. Won his lone attempt at this longer trip and scored a thumping SA Cup win two back. He is a big chance to land another Eureka for the four-year-olds. LOUCASSO (4) has been stunning in winning all six starts here since joining Seaton Grima and was dominant when stepping up to this distance last time. Building an imposing record and is gunning for history as the first three-year-old to win this. The ideal draw gives him every chance to do it. FOX DAN (10) was runner-up in this last year and comes in on a winning note. Showed in his Vicbred win three back he is dangerous with a sit. Can feature again if the race pans out for him. Stablemate CIGANO (12) draws wide but has been building to this, making it three wins in a row when too good here last start. DOUBLE LOU (11) may need luck from the draw but strikes at 50 per cent here so include.

NUTRIEN EQUINE NSW BREEDERS CHALLENGE BLUE - 2YO COLTS & GELDINGS FINAL (GROUP 2) Impossible to go past DON HUNTER (1) from the ace draw. He made it four from four this time in and took his perfect record at this circuit and distance to seven when he led from the middle of the line and was far too good in the heats. Also came from there for a Group 1 win in the Breeders Challenge 2CG Final prior. He can dictate from this draw and should be a class above. FACET PRINCE (5) made it four placings on the trot when he came from this barrier to be beaten less then 2m last time. Solid behind Don Hunter in his previous two. Could chase him home again. RISEABOVETHEREST (4) gets his best draw for some time and overcame a wide barrier to win at this circuit and distance last month. WICKED MOTION (7) draws wider than last start but he did well to finish only 3.3m off Don Hunter there. TIC TIC (9) broke his maiden with a heat win and while drawn wider he has some upside so include.

ULTRA AIR FFA Competitive race but the ace draw should give CAPTAIN BELLASARIO (1) his chance. He has been tackling stronger opposition and was solid enough when fifth last week. Came from wider barriers for back-to-back seconds at this circuit and distance behind Len Smith Mile contenders Hi Manameisjeff and Dangerous last month. Those are good pointers for this. I GOT CHILLS (2) drew widest and worked so was far from disgraced when beaten 6m last time. Up in grade but has won the last four times he has drawn three or lower so will relish this barrier. BETTERTHANCASH (5) hasn't raced since August and is yet to win when fresh but a trial win suggests he is back in good order. This looks a suitable assignment so keep him safe. SAINT CRUSADER (9) may need luck from this barrier but he is going well with placings behind Swayzee and Hi Manameisjeff within his last three starts. Hard to knock the consistency of BUZZ BOMB (8) and he came from wider to win last week so respect. BEST BETS:
